solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Unfinished alcohol etc ruined bar, perhaps (9)

indicatorNotes.Unfinished: the word is left without its last letter
indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: alcohol with its final L cut off
used as printed

annotation.surface: Someone surveys the wreckage of a pub after a night of drink and assorted damage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests the pub of the surface; here it is a bar of chocolate, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Chocolate often comes as a bar, so a bar is one example of it.

entries.clue: What recognises people given cold tea bags? (7)

indicatorNotes.bags: to bag is to capture, so the outer letters take the inner ones into them

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
cha is a slang word for tea
given to doing something = apt to do it

annotation.surface: A question about who gets offered iced tea in bags.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People given cold tea' reads as one phrase, but 'people' ends the definition and 'given' is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A CAPTCHA is the website test that tells human users apart from bots.

entries.clue: Primarily river-based athlete, one going backwards? (3)

blocks.note: a rower can be named after the blade they pull, and rowing is mostly done on rivers
a rower sits facing the stern, so travels backwards

annotation.surface: A sportsman who mostly competes on rivers is described as moving the wrong way.
annotation.walkthrough: An oar can mean a rower, as in 'a good oar'; and a rower sits facing the stern, travelling backwards, which the question mark concedes.
annotation.definitionFit: Oar is used for a rower, who does mostly row on rivers and faces backwards.

entries.clue: Medical examiner turned up like this to handle the situation (8)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning something up reads it bottom to top

blocks.note: so = in this way
used as printed
to cope is to handle what comes

annotation.surface: A coroner arrives dressed this way to take charge of a crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medical examiner' suggests a coroner, but here it is an instrument that examines; 'to' belongs to the turned-up part, not the link.
annotation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the lighted instrument a doctor uses to look into the ear.

entries.clue: School overlooking beginning and end of King Harold (5)

indicatorNotes.overlooking beginning: to overlook is to leave out, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; its H is dropped

annotation.surface: A history lesson about a school that looks down on the demise of the last Saxon king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning and end' looks like a first-and-last-letters instruction; 'and' in fact divides wordplay from definition. King Harold was said to have died from an arrow in the eye at Hastings in 1066.
annotation.definitionFit: Legend has it an arrow in the eye killed Harold at Hastings, so an arrow was his end.

entries.clue: It’s clear retired constituents of Barnet are no xenophobes (9)

indicatorNotes.retired: retiring is withdrawing, drawing back, so the letters are read backwards
indicatorNotes.constituents of: the answer is made up of letters that are parts of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Barnet to the start of xenophobes

annotation.surface: A news line reporting that elderly voters in the London borough of Barnet turn out not to be hostile to foreigners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired constituents' paints pensioner voters, and Barnet is a London borough; in fact 'retired' reverses and 'constituents' points to the letters hidden inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clearing someone of an accusation is exactly what exonerating means.

entries.clue: Small river rod (5)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
the Taff is a river in South Wales, flowing through Cardiff

annotation.surface: A little fishing rod for a small river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a fishing rod to go with the river; it is the definition, a staff.
annotation.definitionFit: A staff is a stick or rod, carried as a support or emblem.

entries.clue: One taking action to restrain very loud bear (6)

indicatorNotes.to restrain: the outer word holds the inner piece in check, around it

blocks.note: a suer is one who takes legal action
ff = fortissimo, very loud in music

annotation.surface: A zookeeper steps in to calm a roaring bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is not the animal but the verb: to put up with something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of putting up with something, as in 'I can't bear it'.

entries.clue: Broadcast, as an example, covers church where Clinton got high (3,5,3)

indicatorNotes.covers: the outer words cover the church, sitting around it

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
'I, for one' = as an example
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: A report on the church where a former US president got high, with a nod to his claim he didn't inhale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Got high' suggests Clinton's famous admission about marijuana; it means flying high in the presidential aircraft.
annotation.definitionFit: Air Force One is the plane the US president flies in, so Clinton was high up in it.

entries.clue: Restless dog shortly to notice yard (7)

indicatorNotes.shortly: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Fido, the stock dog's name, without its O
to get something can be to notice or catch it
y = yard, the unit

annotation.surface: An anxious dog is about to spot something in the yard.
annotation.walkthrough: Fido is the traditional name for a dog, the Rover of crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Fidgety means restless, unable to keep still.

entries.clue: Stop tennis site’s insiders running sport (7)

indicatorNotes.insiders: insiders are those within, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: to park a car is to stop it
a tennis site is a COURT; its inner letters are OUR

annotation.surface: A demand that insiders at a tennis venue quit their jogging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running' seems to go with the insiders of the surface; it belongs to the definition, since parkour is a sport of running and jumping.
annotation.definitionFit: Parkour is a sport of running, climbing and vaulting over urban obstacles.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t complete crossword here, away from civilisation (3-4)

blocks.note: read literally: outside the grid of squares
living without mains power, water or gas

annotation.surface: Advice that a remote retreat is no place for puzzle-solving.
annotation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: writing off the grid won't complete a crossword. Off-grid also means living without mains utilities.
annotation.definitionFit: Off-grid life is lived away from mains power and so away from civilisation.

entries.clue: Youngster in charge of power? (5)

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout
i/c = in charge

annotation.surface: A question whether a youth should be given authority.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power' seems political; in maths a power is an exponent, and cubic is the third power, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Cubic refers to the third power, as in a cubic equation.

entries.clue: Aquatic plant’s book value cut by 20 per cent after damage to hose? (11)

indicatorNotes.cut by 20 per cent: a five-letter word loses one of its five letters, a fifth of it
indicatorNotes.after: in a down clue this piece comes after the damage

blocks.note: b = book
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings
WORTH with its last letter, one fifth, cut

annotation.surface: A pond plant's worth is marked down by a fifth after it damages a garden hose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden hose; it is old-fashioned for stockings, where a ladder is a run. The 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Bladderwort is a carnivorous water plant that traps prey in tiny bladders.

entries.clue: Miserable single on Web receiving love, say (9)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the single comes on after the rest
indicatorNotes.receiving: the web takes the love into itself

blocks.note: used as printed
love = zero in tennis, O
e.g. = say, for example
single = one

annotation.surface: A lonely singleton goes online hoping to be sent some love.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints online dating; 'single' is just ONE, placed at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Woebegone means sad and miserable in appearance.

entries.clue: Accountant rejected person in high court ignoring books without backing (1,8)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected = thrown back, so the letters are reversed
indicatorNotes.ignoring: the books are left out of the word

blocks.note: CA = chartered accountant
an appellant brings an appeal before a higher court
NT = New Testament, a set of books; removed

annotation.surface: An accountant's appeal is thrown out by a court that disregards his books and gives him no support.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' look like accounts, fitting the accountant; they are the New Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed without instrumental backing.

entries.clue: One pound in Omani currency raised — it’s been brought to a new state (6,3)

annotation.definition: it’s been brought to a new state

indicatorNotes.in: the pound goes inside the currency
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word reads it upwards

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
a quid is British slang for a pound
the rial is Oman's currency

annotation.surface: A currency report says a pound's value has risen against the Omani rial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' seems political after the currency talk; it is a state of matter, gas turned liquid.
annotation.definitionFit: Liquid air is air cooled until it changes from gas to liquid, a new state of matter.

entries.clue: Nauseating bow tie repels daughter (4)

indicatorNotes.repels: the word drives the letter out

blocks.note: a dicky bow is British slang for a bow tie
d = daughter; driven out

annotation.surface: A daughter recoils from her father's sickly bow tie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repels' reads as disgust, which suits the surface; here it means pushing the D out of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Icky means sickly or distasteful.

entries.clue: Suppose American cooked dishes (3,5)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooked = worked over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
A = American

annotation.surface: A guess about what an American chef made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' sits naturally beside the chef of the surface, which hides its role as the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: soups are dishes, and pea soup is one kind.

entries.clue: Hoax letter in particular case for Endeavour Morse? (4)

indicatorNotes.letter in particular case for: upper case is a particular case, and Endeavour's capital letter is its E

blocks.note: cod means fake, a hoax
the initial capital of Endeavour

annotation.surface: A fake letter becomes evidence in a case for the TV detective Endeavour Morse.
annotation.walkthrough: Endeavour Morse is the detective of the TV series Inspector Morse and Endeavour; the definition is only 'Morse', the telegraph code, and the question mark marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Samuel Morse's system of dots and dashes is one code among many.

entries.clue: Doctor admitting staff following carbon monoxide rule (7)

indicatorNotes.admitting: the doctor lets the staff in, around it
indicatorNotes.following: the doctor part comes after carbon monoxide

blocks.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
MD = Doctor of Medicine
to staff a post is to man it

annotation.surface: A hospital rule after a gas poisoning case: a doctor must take in the staff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun, employees; it is the verb, to man.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: a ruler commands a country.

entries.clue: Canadian green bisque ruined sandwiches (9)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rearranged
indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the rearranged letters sit either side of the green, like bread

blocks.note: anagram fodder
eco = green, environmentally friendly

annotation.surface: A Canadian cook spoils a soup by making sandwiches of it.
annotation.walkthrough: Bisque is a creamy soup, which gives the kitchen surface; Québécois is French for someone from Quebec.
annotation.definitionFit: A Québécois is a Canadian from Quebec, usually French-speaking.

entries.clue: Where one may lie, mostly to date teacher (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the phrase is kept, the last letter goes

blocks.note: so far = to date, missing its last letter
a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

annotation.surface: Gossip that someone has mostly lied about dating a teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests an untruth next to 'date'; it is lying down on a bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: a couch that unfolds for sleeping is one place a person can stretch out.

entries.clue: Largely obscure recurring complaint (6)

indicatorNotes.Largely: most of the word is kept, its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.recurring: the piece occurs again, so it is written twice

blocks.note: murk, as an adjective, means dark and obscure; its K is dropped

annotation.surface: A doctor notes a mostly unexplained ailment that keeps coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as an illness, suiting 'recurring', and a heart murmur is one; but it also means a muttered grumble.
annotation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low grumble of complaint, or a heart murmur, a medical complaint.

entries.clue: Temperamental soldier hired uniform before retreat back (9)

indicatorNotes.before: the pieces come before the retreat

blocks.note: merc is short for mercenary, a hired soldier
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet
a lair is a hideaway

annotation.surface: A moody mercenary puts on his uniform before pulling back to base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the soldier's kit; it is just the letter U.
annotation.definitionFit: Mercurial means changeable and unpredictable in mood.

entries.clue: Feature of extremely rich poem (5)

indicatorNotes.Feature of: the answer is featured inside the following words

blocks.note: extremeLY RICh

annotation.surface: A description of what makes a poem lavish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'rich', and 'Feature' like a quality of the poem; together they only house the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing feeling.

entries.clue: Rack where flesh gets torn (5)

indicatorNotes.gets torn: the word is ripped apart and its letters reordered

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A torture chamber where the rack rips a victim's flesh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rack' conjures the torture device; it is a set of shelves.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym for storage: a rack holding books or plates works as a shelf.

entries.clue: Regressive plans supported by a lack of sense (7)

indicatorNotes.Regressive: going backwards, so the whole wordplay is read in reverse

blocks.note: aims = plans
to rest on something is to be supported by it
used as printed

annotation.surface: A complaint that backward-looking policies are propped up by foolishness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lack of sense' reads as foolishness; the sense is smell.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: the Greek roots mean 'without smell', so the missing sense is the nose's.

entries.clue: Regret insult overheard in staged conversation? (7)

indicatorNotes.overheard: what is heard, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: rue = regret, barb = insult

annotation.surface: Someone regrets an insult caught on stage in a scripted exchange.
annotation.walkthrough: Actors in a crowd scene mutter 'rhubarb' to fake background chatter; the question mark marks this as a playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is the word extras repeat to mimic conversation on stage.

entries.clue: Feel sick of ’orrible weather (3)

indicatorNotes.’orrible: the apostrophe shows a dropped H, so the weather loses its H too

blocks.note: hail is a kind of weather, spoken without its H

annotation.surface: A Cockney complains of feeling sick of the horrible weather.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''orrible' shows the Cockney habit of dropping H, and the solver applies it to HAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned verb: to ail is to be poorly, as in 'what ails you?'

entries.clue: Ruminant taking time to stop (5)

indicatorNotes.taking: the ruminant takes the time into itself

blocks.note: a deer chews the cud, a ruminant
t = time

annotation.surface: A cud-chewing animal takes its time to come to a halt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking time' reads as dawdling; it means the T goes inside the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to deter someone is to stop them acting, by discouragement.

entries.clue: Hard music genre with new idols (4-5)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: rock music
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Heavy music with a fresh batch of pop idols.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard' seems to describe the music, as in hard rock; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means completely hard and firm.
